prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the project's two Umbraco MCP servers, umbraco and umbraco-editor.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP servers won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP servers.

Always use the MCP servers to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Done — uSync has exported all schema automatically. The site is running and everything works. Final report:

## What was built

**Schema (via the `umbraco` MCP server):**
- **Element types** in `Blocks/`: `heroBlock` (heading, subheading, image), `textBlock` (richtext), `imageTextBlock` (image + richtext + credit)
- **Page types** in `Pages/`: `blogFrontPage` (heading, intro, blocks; allows `blogPost` children), `blogPost` (excerpt, blocks)
- **Data type**: `Blog Block Grid` (Umbraco.BlockGrid, 12 columns, all three blocks registered), used by both pages' `blocks` property
- **Templates**: `blogFrontPage`, `blogPost`; `siteRoot` updated to allow `blogFrontPage` children
- **Domains**: `/` assigned to the Blog page per the repository rule
- **Media**: `Blog` folder with all 10 Unsplash photos imported via `create-media-multiple`

**Content (via the `umbraco-editor` MCP server):**
- **Blog** front page — hero block (heading, subheading, network-graph background image) + a post listing
- **"Why MCP is awesome: one protocol, every tool"** — image-text block (orange USB cables) + two rich-text blocks on the M×N problem
- **"Why MCP is awesome: agents that can actually help"** — rich-text + image-text block (puzzle piece) + a closing "this post is the demo" section
- All published; block payloads verified read-back after each write

**Razor (after the build/restart, per the required order):**
- `_Layout.cshtml` (Tailwind dark theme), page views render blocks with `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync` — no custom loop
- Adapter partials `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{heroBlock,textBlock,imageTextBlock}.cshtml` → plain models (`Models/Blocks/`) → ViewComponents `Hero`, `Text`, `ImageText` with all markup in their component views
- Frontend bundle built (`site.css` Tailwind scanning Razor views, `main.js`)

## How to view it

Umbraco is still running (background `dotnet run` in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco`):
- **http://localhost:41576/** — front page with hero + post list
- http://localhost:41576/why-mcp-is-awesome-one-protocol-every-tool/
- http://localhost:41576/why-mcp-is-awesome-agents-that-can-actually-help/

Verified with curl: 200 on the pages, CSS, and signed media URLs; hero/image-text blocks render with images and credits.

## Not working / caveats

- Nothing broken that I found. `publishedUrls` in MCP publish responses stays empty and preview URLs require backoffice auth, but direct HTTP checks confirm the published site.
- Pre-existing build warnings only (e.g. NU1902 SixLabors.ImageSharp advisory) — untouched.
- `textBlock`/`imageTextBlock` render full-bleed 12-column rows via Umbraco's grid chrome; fine for this demo, but the shipped `blockgrid/default.cshtml` would need the sanctioned local edits if narrower gutters were wanted.
- uSync auto-exported all six content types, templates, and the block grid data type to `uSync/v18/` as required by rule 10.
